name: tarantool
desc: In-memory database and Lua application server
why: An in-memory database that doubles as a Lua application server, a database with a twist worth poking at.

brief.what_it_is: Tarantool is an in-memory computing platform made of a database and an application server, distributed under BSD 2-Clause. The database keeps data in RAM, with WAL-based persistence, and offers HASH, TREE, RTREE and BITSET indexes, MessagePack data and client-server protocol, and ANSI SQL. The application server runs Lua (LuaJIT 2.1 with a tracing JIT) inside the same process, with cooperative multitasking and non-blocking IO, plus built-in persistent queues, sharding, and a cluster management framework. Data goes in through the database API, SQL, or Lua code, and results come back to clients or to the application logic running alongside the data.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage pitches it as a fast in-memory store that also fixes the usual weakness of RAM-only databases, which is losing data on failure or restart. The README frames it as a platform for data-enriched parts of scalable web architecture, such as queue servers, caches, and stateful web applications.
brief.how_it_works: Code and data share one address space, so Lua logic runs next to the stored data instead of across a network hop. Writes go to a write-ahead log and the transaction result returns only after it is saved to disk. The homepage also describes synchronous and asynchronous replication, and an MVCC transaction mode.
brief.install_notes: The README points to the download page for binary packages for your OS and to Docker images, and to the Tarantool documentation for building from source. Supported platforms are Linux (x86_64, aarch64), macOS (x86_64 and M1), and FreeBSD (x86_64). Extra modules and connectors come from the rocks repository, the connectors page, and the Awesome Tarantool list. I did not read the install page itself, so there are no first-run steps or config details in these notes.
brief.standout: It is a database and an application server in one process: the Lua code and the data share an address space, and the database is a C extension that can be switched off. Most in-memory stores are only a cache or a key-value store, so this combination is the unusual part.
brief.status: Looks maintained, though I could not confirm a date. The docs nav lists releases up to Tarantool 3.7 and a 'latest (3.x)' version selector, and the GitHub README has active CI, coverage, and OSS-Fuzz badges. I did not see a last-commit or last-release date, so the exact status is unknown.
brief.caveats: The homepage is a marketing page for the Community Edition, and the owner is VK LLC. Its claims about replication lag and near-zero data loss are vendor copy, not measured results. Enterprise-only products, such as Tarantool Enterprise, Data Grid, and Cluster Manager, are mixed into the same navigation, so check which features are in the Community build. Platform support is limited to Linux, macOS, and FreeBSD, with no Windows listed in what I read.
quotes: Tarantool is an in-memory computing platform consisting of a database and an application server.
The database is a C extension of the application server and can be turned off.
Tarantool is ideal for data-enriched components of scalable Web architecture: queue servers, caches, stateful Web applications.
Tarantool keeps all the data in random-access memory (RAM). Solutions of this class are fast, but they often lack data persistence. Tarantool solves this problem.
fetch_log: https://tarantool.org/ — worked, but it is a marketing page with no README or commands; it lists the product and docs navigation and says data is kept in RAM with WAL persistence.
https://github.com/tarantool/tarantool — worked, returned the README with the feature list, platforms, license, and links to download and build instructions.
https://www.tarantool.io/en/doc/latest/getting_started/ — worked, but it is mostly site navigation with a short overview and no shell commands.
